description: Linux kernel audit framework that logs syscalls, file access, authentication events, and security-relevant operations. Provides forensic trail and can trigger alerts.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: Compensating control: attacker actions are logged and may trigger alerting

verification.method: Verify auditd is running with rules loaded

remediation.name: Enable auditd with base security audit rules

steps.description: Enable and start the auditd service so audit events are captured immediately and on every boot
Write base audit rules covering sensitive file access, privileged command execution, and kernel module loading to a drop-in rules file
steps.command:
cat > /etc/audit/rules.d/99-cme-1002.rules <<'EOF'
## Sensitive file access
-w /etc/shadow -p wa -k shadow_access
-w /etc/passwd -p wa -k passwd_access
-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k sudoers_access
-w /etc/sudoers.d/ -p wa -k sudoers_access

## Privileged command execution
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -F euid=0 -F auid>=1000 -F auid!=unset -k priv_exec
-a always,exit -F arch=b32 -S execve -F euid=0 -F auid>=1000 -F auid!=unset -k priv_exec

## Kernel module loading
-w /sbin/insmod -p x -k module_load
-w /sbin/modprobe -p x -k module_load
-w /sbin/rmmod -p x -k module_load
-a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S init_module,finit_module,delete_module -k module_load
EOF

steps.description: Load the new audit rules into the running kernel audit subsystem
